statement: Positive integers $x$ and $y$ satisfy $x^2 - y^2 = 45$. What is the sum of all possible values of $x$?

choices.misconception: I used only the factor pair 1 × 45, which gives x = 23 and y = 22, and missed the other pairs.
I used the pairs 1 × 45 and 5 × 9 but missed 3 × 15, so I added only 23 + 7.
I used the pairs 1 × 45 and 3 × 15 but missed 5 × 9, so I added only 23 + 9.
I added the sums of the factor pairs, 46 + 18 + 14 = 78, but each of those sums is (x - y) + (x + y) = 2x, so I needed to halve them.

hints: Factor the left side as a difference of squares.
$(x - y)(x + y) = 45$, and $x + y$ is bigger than $x - y$.
The factor pairs of $45$ are $1 \times 45$, $3 \times 15$ and $5 \times 9$. In each pair, $x$ is the average of the two factors.

solutions.reliable: Since $(x - y)(x + y) = 45$ with $0 < x - y < x + y$, the pair $(x - y, x + y)$ is $(1, 45)$, $(3, 15)$ or $(5, 9)$. In each case $x$ is the average of the two factors, giving $x = 23$, $9$ or $7$, with $y = 22$, $6$ or $2$. All three work; for example, $9^2 - 6^2 = 81 - 36 = 45$. The sum of the possible values of $x$ is $23 + 9 + 7 = 39$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
